chunks: My father (peace be upon him) and a group of my companions (peace be upon him) narrated from Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā and Aḥmad ibn Idrīs, all from al-‘Amrakī ibn ‘Alī, from Yaḥyā the servant of Abī Ja‘far the Second (peace be upon him), from Muḥammad ibn Sinān, from Bashīr al-Dahhān, who said:

I heard Abā ‘Abdillāh (peace be upon him) saying while he was staying in al-Ḥīrah, with a group of the Shī‘ah around him. He turned his face toward me and said, 'O Bashīr! Did you perform Ḥajj this year?' I replied, 'May I be sacrificed for you! No, but I spent ‘Arafah at the grave—the grave of al-Ḥusain (peace be upon him).' He said, 'O Bashīr! By Allāh, you did not miss anything of what the people of Ḥajj received in Makkah.' I said, 'May I be sacrificed for you! ‘Arafah is only in Makkah, so explain this to me.' He said, 'O Bashīr! Verily, a man among you performs Ghusl on the shore of the Euphrates, then goes to the grave of al-Ḥusain (peace be upon him), knowing his rights. Allāh grants him for every step he raises or places one hundred accepted Ḥajj, one hundred purified ‘Umrah, and one hundred battles alongside a sent Prophet against the enemies of Allāh and the enemies of His Messenger. O Bashīr! Listen and convey to those whose hearts can bear it: Whoever visits al-Ḥusain (peace be upon him) on the Day of ‘Arafah is like one who visits Allāh on His Throne.'

key_terms.الْحِيرَة: Al-Hīrah, a city in Iraq where Imam al-Ṣādiq stayed
key_terms.زِيَارَة: Visit (specifically to the graves of Imams or saints)
key_terms.عَرَفْتُ بِالْقَبْرِ: Spent ‘Arafah at the grave (referring to the day of pilgrimage)
key_terms.قَبْرَ الْحُسَيْنِ: The grave of al-Ḥusain (peace be upon him)

ai.seo_question: What is the reward for visiting Imam Husain's grave on the Day of Arafah?
ai.summary: Imam al-Ṣādiq (peace be upon him) elevates the Ziyārah of Imām al-Ḥusain (peace be upon him) on the Day of ‘Arafah to the status of a superior pilgrimage, promising that every step taken yields the reward of a hundred accepted Ḥajjāt, ‘Umrahs, and Ghazwāt alongside a Messenger of God. This tradition, recorded by Ibn Qulawayh, underscores the Shia theological concept of the Imams as the spiritual centers of the earth, where visiting the grave of the Imam is equated to 'visiting God on His Throne,' thereby linking the cosmic authority of the Ahl al-Bayt directly to divine presence. The emphasis on ritual purification by the Euphrates (Dajlah) further connects the physical act of Ziyārah to the sacred geography of Karbala, reinforcing the continuity of the Prophet’s legacy through the Imams.
